purpose: Chrome (MV3) proxy manager: pairs every proxy with a coherent, country-matched privacy fingerprint (identity) + WebRTC/DNS leak protection, so each account looks like its own real device.

deployment.note: Chrome Web Store live (v1.23.8, id ceobadpmhnfmlndkcmobhejkmbjimmcj); Edge Add-ons in review; GitHub Releases zip for unpacked/developer installs. No server in THIS repo — payments/landing run in the separate private proxybro-worker repo.

stack: Chrome MV3 (service worker, no build step)
Cloudflare Workers (license validation + landing, external, private repo)

entrypoints.name: Load unpacked (dev)
entrypoints.how: chrome://extensions -> Developer mode -> Load unpacked -> this folder -> enable 'Allow user scripts' in the extension's Details

entrypoints.name: Popup UI harness (no install needed)
entrypoints.how: open harness.html directly in a normal browser tab — it mocks chrome.* and loads popup.html+popup.js so popup logic runs outside the extension context

components.name: Popup UI
components.does: Identity (profile) list + editor, bulk proxy import (any-format auto-detect), advanced per-field fingerprint editor, Diagnostics tab (exit IP/WebRTC/coherence probes against cloudflare-trace/ipwho.is/ipify), Free/Pro paywall + Creem license-key activation UI. Free = 1 identity (profiles.length gate), extras locked not deleted.

components.name: Background Service Worker
components.does: Owns all privacy mechanics: proxy activation (chrome.proxy.settings), WebRTC leak policy (chrome.privacy.network.webRTCIPHandlingPolicy), DNS hardening (DoH + prefetch-off while proxied), fail-closed fingerprint activation (won't turn on a spoofing identity unless the document_start user-script path is confirmed live), declarativeNetRequest rules (MV3 replacement for blocking webRequest), and registers the MAIN-world document_start user script that installs the fingerprint overrides before any page script runs.

components.name: Extension Manifest
components.does: Declares permissions (proxy, storage, webRequest(AuthProvider), privacy, userScripts, scripting, declarativeNetRequest, tabs, cookies, notifications, alarms, browsingData), host_permissions (<all_urls> + https://ipwho.is/*), service_worker entry (background.js), popup entry (popup.html), icon set, current version (source of truth for the version badge in README).

components.name: user-agents.json
components.does: OS/browser-keyed user-agent strings (chrome_windows/mac/linux, firefox_*, safari_mac, edge_windows, mobile_safari) fetched by popup-ui at runtime via chrome.runtime.getURL to build the country-matched fingerprint options. Part of the Store zip (shipped).

components.name: Popup Test Harness
components.tech: hand-rolled chrome.* mock, no test framework
components.does: Mocks chrome.storage/runtime/proxy/privacy/tabs/scripting/declarativeNetRequest/cookies/browsingData/notifications/action/webNavigation with a controllable window.__mock state, then loads popup.html+popup.js so real popup logic runs against the mock. Driven from outside via preview_eval to assert STATE TRANSITIONS, not just syntax — this is the pre-push gate together with `node --check`.
components.verify: open harness.html in a plain tab, drive via console, check window.__ready === true

components.name: Leak & Fingerprint Test Suite
components.does: Dev-only QA page (excluded from the Store zip): probes WebRTC candidate IPs, canvas/WebGL fingerprint, timezone/language the same way an external tracker would, so a developer can manually confirm ProxyBro's protections hold while it's active.
components.verify: open test/leak-test.html with ProxyBro active, compare readouts to Diagnostics tab

components.name: creem-worker.js (reference copy)
components.does: A minimal REFERENCE implementation of the Creem license-activation endpoint (POST /validate -> Creem /v1/licenses/activate, holds CREEM_API_KEY server-side so the extension never ships it). Committed since v1.19.0, unmodified since — kept as documentation of the mechanism. NOT the deployed worker: the real, richer one (referral, feedback D1, rate-limit bindings) lives in the separate PRIVATE proxybro-worker repo and is what popup-ui actually calls.

components.name: proxybro-worker (external, private repo)
components.tech: Cloudflare Workers + D1, separate PRIVATE repo humanperzeus/proxybro-worker
components.does: Serves proxybro.app (landing, /buy, /check leak-test, /config) and the real /validate + /deactivate license endpoints popup-ui calls. Holds the Creem API keys server-side. Payment mode-flip, admin paths and secret names are documented in THAT repo's own docs/architecture.json, never here (public repo).

components.name: Creem
components.does: Payment + license-key provider. $5/mo or $30/yr Pro plan. Extension never talks to Creem directly — only proxybro-worker holds the API key and activates/validates keys server-side.
components.verify: n/a — third-party SaaS status page only

components.name: IP/Geo probe services
components.does: Three independent exit-IP/country probes (first-ok wins) used both for Diagnostics (popup-ui) and for auto-generating a country-matched fingerprint + timezone/language self-heal (background-worker). ipwho.is is the one declared in host_permissions; the others ride on <all_urls>.

components.name: Chrome Web Store
components.does: Auto-updating distribution channel for end users (id ceobadpmhnfmlndkcmobhejkmbjimmcj). GitHub Releases zip is the manual/unpacked alternative; Latest-only policy (older release assets deleted on each new tag).

components.name: ProxyBro-marketing (external, no git)
components.does: Marketing assets (demo video 'proxybro advertise.mp4') referenced from the README/landing; lives in a sibling folder with no git repo of its own.

dataflows.what: Diagnostics probes: cloudflare cdn-cgi/trace, ipwho.is, api.ipify.org (first-ok wins)
dataflows.when: Diagnostics tab open or exit-IP check

dataflows.what: exit IP/country lookup through the active proxy, used to auto-heal timezone/language/fingerprint coherence
registers/updates a MAIN-world document_start chrome.userScripts entry (id pb-spoof) that installs the fingerprint overrides before page scripts run
dataflows.when: spoofing settings change while a proxy/identity is active

dataflows.what: server-side license activation (POST /v1/licenses/activate with the secret API key)

agent_notes: This is a PUBLIC repo — CLAUDE.md and STACK.md (the private ops docs with live payment mode, worker deploy commands, secret NAMES) are gitignored on purpose. Never add payment/admin mechanics (endpoints, mode-flip vars, secret names) to THIS architecture.json — that belongs in the private proxybro-worker repo's own map. Extension itself ships with ZERO secrets (hard rule, enforced: grep the diff before any commit).

creem-worker.js in this repo is a REFERENCE copy only (unmodified since v1.19.0) — the actually-deployed license-validation worker (richer: D1 feedback, referral, rate-limit) lives in the separate PRIVATE proxybro-worker repo. Don't assume creem-worker.js is what's live.

Fail-closed invariant: proxy ON for a spoofing identity implies the reliable document_start user-script path is confirmed live (chrome.userScripts present) — background.js disconnects instead of falling back to a racy executeScript path that could leak the real fingerprint. Needs Chrome's per-extension 'Allow user scripts' toggle; without it, spoofing simply won't activate (by design, not a bug).

DNS-leak model (CLAUDE.md §9 resolution-model class): DoH is NOT proxy-tunneled — it hides DNS from the local network but still resolves from the REAL IP. True exit-country DNS only comes from an HTTP/SOCKS5 proxy scheme (the proxy resolves). DoH is force-enabled ONLY for SOCKS4 (which has no remote DNS at all — DoH beats a plaintext local-ISP leak there); for HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS5 DoH stays OFF so Chrome hands DNS to the proxy. Forcing DoH globally would be the wrong lever (competes with the goal path) — see background.js:429-451.

popup.js has a real top-level-vs-`setupEventListeners` scope rule: a function called from BOTH initialize() and an event listener MUST be declared top-level, or it ReferenceErrors at runtime. Gate is `node --check popup.js` (syntax) PLUS harness.html driven through real state transitions (syntax-only checks miss this class of bug).

Store build = exactly 9 files: manifest.json, popup.html, popup.js, background.js, user-agents.json, icons/icon{16,32,48,128}.png. Everything else (test/, docs/, README, harness.html, creem-worker.js, redesign-mockup.html) is dev-only and excluded from the release zip.

MV3 forbids blocking webRequest — all request blocking/header rewriting uses dynamic declarativeNetRequest rules; webRequest is kept ONLY for onAuthRequired (proxy authentication), which MV3 still allows.

Free = 1 identity, enforced by `profiles.length >= 1` gates in popup.js (not a separate MAX_ constant) — locked (not deleted) identities beyond the first stay in storage so nothing is lost if the user later goes Pro.
Never claim simultaneous multi-account isolation in copy/UI — one browser = one cookie jar, ProxyBro is honestly sequential (one identity at a time), not a full anti-detect browser.
conventions: No BRAIN.md in this repo — README.md + TODO.md + (gitignored) STACK.md/CLAUDE.md are the status docs; TODO.md tracks Next/Done, STACK.md (private) tracks live infra/payment mode.
One unit = one branch; never merge without an explicit 'go merge' (CLAUDE.md §3).
Gate before any push: `node --check popup.js` (+ background.js/creem-worker.js by extension) plus harness.html driven over real state transitions, not just syntax.

Two moving parts, two repos: this repo is the extension only; the worker+landing+payments backend is a separate PRIVATE repo (proxybro-worker) — the extension only ever calls proxybro.app/buy and /validate.
